_meta.source: Port pin is the Port Est industrial area from OpenStreetMap. Every POI was resolved individually against OpenStreetMap via Nominatim on 2026-07-30 — none is estimated off a street map. Unlike most port maps this one deliberately spans the whole island, because on Réunion the island IS the decision space: the page's central argument is about drive times, and a map that hid Cilaos and the volcano off the edge would hide the argument. Note that the L'Hermitage pin resolves to the historic chimneys in the village rather than to the beach itself.

port_pin.label: Port Est — the cruise berth, Le Port

bbox_hint.note: Le Port and Port Est are on the dry north-west coast. Saint-Gilles and the lagoon are 20 km south, Saint-Denis 22 km north-east. Cilaos, Piton des Neiges and Hell-Bourg are in the mountainous interior; Piton de la Fournaise is at the far south-east of the island, two and a half hours away by road.

pois.name: Port Est — cruise berth
pois.notes: Cruise ships berth alongside at the gare maritime. No tendering. Channel dredged to 16 m; a 648 m quay works two 80,000-tonne ships at once. Free wifi in the terminal.

pois.name: Le Port
pois.notes: The port town itself. A working commune rather than a destination — everything you came for is elsewhere on the island.

pois.name: Saint-Gilles-les-Bains
pois.notes: The west-coast resort strip, about 20 km and 18 minutes from the berth. The helicopter operators fly from here, and the lagoon is here. The practical centre of a Réunion port day.

pois.name: L'Hermitage-les-Bains
pois.notes: The lagoon behind the fringing reef — one of the few places on this coast where swimming is legal. The protection is the reef itself, and it ends where the reef ends.

pois.name: Saint-Paul
pois.notes: The commune between Le Port and Saint-Gilles, and the island's first European settlement.

pois.name: Saint-Denis
pois.notes: The capital, 15-25 minutes north on the coastal motorway. Creole colonial architecture on the rue de Paris, the Jardin de l'État, the Grande Mosquée Noor-e-Islam, the Barachois seafront.

pois.name: Le Maïdo
pois.notes: A belvedere at 2,200 m looking straight down into Mafate — the best free view on the island. It clouds over by mid-morning almost every day, so go at dawn.

pois.name: Piton des Neiges
pois.notes: 3,070 m, the highest point in the Indian Ocean. A dormant volcano whose collapsed and eroded flanks are the three cirques.

pois.name: Cilaos
pois.notes: Reached only by the RN5, the road of 400 bends — 35 km of hairpins and single-lane rock tunnels from Saint-Louis up past 1,200 m. Two to two and a half hours each way from the berth, and closure-prone in the wet season. Thermal springs, lentils, and France's highest vineyard.

pois.name: Hell-Bourg
pois.notes: A village of restored Creole houses in the Cirque de Salazie, listed among France's plus beaux villages. About two hours each way — the achievable cirque from this berth.

pois.name: Trou de Fer
pois.notes: A gorge nearly 300 m deep holding four waterfalls, in the Salazie massif. There is a land belvedere via the Bélouve forest, but the full amphitheatre is an aerial sight — which is why every helicopter operator sells it as the centrepiece.

pois.name: Piton de la Fournaise
pois.notes: One of the world's most active volcanoes — two eruptions in the first four months of 2026, the second running 58 days and building 8.5 ha of new land into the sea. About 2h30 each way by road from Le Port. Access to the enclos is by prefectural order and closes when the alert rises.
